page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.12xlarge is a general-purpose, network and EBS-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARM64 architecture with AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 (ARMv9) processors running at 2.8 GHz. The processor configuration provides one thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1D cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but it delivers a high baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates highly competitive multi-core and memory performance. The m8gn.12xlarge achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core execution, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark database operations. Its memory subsystem is highly efficient, scoring in the top tier for uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth, as well as overall Passmark memory metrics. Single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the average tier. For specialized workloads, static web serving throughput is in the top tier, and Redis SET operations perform in the strong top 25% tier. Large language model inference text generation for medium and large models is strong, though text generation for very small models is relatively weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8gn.12xlarge leverages the ARM64 Graviton architecture to deliver high multi-core resource density and exceptional memory bandwidth without the premium associated with x86 hardware classes. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, relying entirely on EBS. This instance is highly suited for multi-threaded workloads, including software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and medium-to-large scale LLM text generation.
